title: Organisms grow along stream lines definable by a mathematical transformation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Organisms grow along stream lines definable by a mathematical transformation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The law of growth implied by representing related forms as orthogonal coordinate transformations is that the organism grows along stream lines definable by a suitable mathematical transformation; departures from orthogonality reflect the organism not being homogeneous and isotropic.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the “law of growth” which our biological analysis by means of orthogonal co-ordinate systems presupposes, or at least foreshadows, is one according to which the organism grows or develops along _stream lines_, which may be defined by a suitable mathematical transformation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Stream lines and law of growth”. Scope: growth of organisms in general

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-09: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.32

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A restricted version is measurable, but the general claim does not specify the transformation or a unique decision criterion. Existing developmental movies cover small systems and cannot address organisms in general.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate cell or tissue trajectories from dense developmental time series and ask whether one prespecified transformation produces streamlines matching those trajectories, with non-orthogonality predicted by measured anisotropy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Organism-wide time-resolved deformation and material anisotropy are unavailable.

“Suitable transformation” is flexible enough to fit trajectories post hoc.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.28
analysis feasibility: 0.38
data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stream lines are a redescription of whatever displacement field the organism shows once a coordinate map has been fitted. Departures from orthogonality are assigned to the tissue not being homogeneous. That structure has no measurable outcome that would count against the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says organisms grow along stream lines of a suitable transformation, with non-orthogonal cases explained by inhomogeneity. Because the transformation is chosen to fit the growth, every smooth growth field satisfies the description, and no public dataset can separate it from a rival growth law.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Cell-tracking volumes exist for a few model embryos and still leave the transformation free to be chosen afterward.
